entrypoints.summary: A GET request supplies the madness parameter, which is interpolated into the php://filter wrapper path.

affected_components.role: Constructs and consumes the request-influenced PHP stream-wrapper URI and conditionally reads the flag.
Places the conditional-read target at /flag.txt in the container.

causal_paths.kind: request parameter to interpreted wrapper path
sentinel comparison to secret response content

negative_controls: The source dies on a literal slash in madness.
The source dies when the constructed wrapper path exceeds 100 characters.
A transformed result other than the sentinel leaves the flag-read branch unselected.
observability.positive_marker: The source renders the result variable; only the sentinel-equality branch replaces it with content read from /flag.txt.

preconditions: The service must run the supplied PHP application with PHP stream wrappers available.
A request value would need to satisfy the source checks: no literal slash and a constructed wrapper URI length no greater than 100 characters.
Sentinel reachability by an allowed PHP filter-chain value is not established by the supplied artifacts.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A filter-specification segment without a literal slash; no working value is supplied.
trigger_steps.summary: Submit an HTTP GET request carrying a candidate madness filter-specification value that conforms to the literal-slash and constructed-length checks.

impacts.concept: conditional HTTP disclosure of secret-file contents

mitigations.concept: fixed or allowlisted PHP filter configuration
remove secret-file read from transformed-output branch

relation_candidates.rationale: The madness GET value is concatenated into the php://filter specification before the wrapper is passed to file_get_contents.
The transformed result is compared to a fixed sentinel, and equality selects the branch that reads /flag.txt. Reaching equality with an allowed filter chain is not demonstrated in the bundle.

relation_candidates.dst: conditional HTTP disclosure of secret-file contents
relation_candidates.rationale: The selected branch assigns file_get_contents('/flag.txt') to the response result, which is then echoed; the image copies flag.txt to /flag.txt.

relation_candidates.dst: fixed or allowlisted PHP filter configuration
relation_candidates.rationale: Replacing direct concatenation of madness into the php://filter specification with a fixed configuration or an allowlisted selection would prevent request syntax from selecting the interpreted filter chain. No patch is supplied.

relation_candidates.dst: remove secret-file read from transformed-output branch
relation_candidates.rationale: Removing the coded branch that reads /flag.txt when transformed content equals the sentinel would remove this conditional secret-read capability. No patch is supplied.

impact.affected_asset: The /flag.txt file copied into the container image.
impact.attacker_capability: Potentially choose a PHP filter-chain transformation for the fixed /etc/passwd resource and, if a permitted chain produces the sentinel, trigger the conditional flag-file read.
impact.security_effect: Conditional disclosure of the container's /flag.txt content through the rendered HTTP response.

causal_trace.summary: The HTTP GET parameter madness is read from the request and is attacker-controlled.

The handler rejects literal slash characters and paths longer than 100 characters, but otherwise concatenates madness into the filter-specification position of a php://filter wrapper; the wrapper interpreter, rather than an allowlist, defines the accepted filter segment.
file_get_contents consumes the constructed attacker-influenced php://filter URI, with /etc/passwd fixed as the wrapper resource.

If the resulting transformed content is exactly the sentinel string "zombies for the flag", the handler reads /flag.txt and renders that content in the HTTP response. The container definition places flag.txt at /flag.txt.

failure.operation: file_get_contents($file) on an attacker-influenced php://filter URI, followed by the sentinel-gated /flag.txt read

primary_invariant.statement: Untrusted request text must not select or construct a PHP stream-filter specification that is interpreted by file_get_contents; any permitted transformation must be fixed or selected from an explicit allowlist independent of attacker syntax.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The madness value is concatenated directly after php://filter/ and before resource=/etc/passwd, so it occupies the stream wrapper's filter-specification segment. The code's literal-slash blacklist and URI-length limit do not establish that this segment is a fixed or allowlisted filter configuration.

quality.review_notes: The primary source and container configuration establish the request-to-wrapper-to-sentinel branch structurally. No supplied payload, solver writeup, runtime trace, or execution result demonstrates that a slash-free, length-bounded filter chain can produce the sentinel under PHP 8.2.2. No fixed implementation or remediation patch is present; mitigation statements and graph revocation edges are unimplemented, source-derived repair proposals. The bundled redacted flag is an intended oracle artifact rather than proof of exploitation.

remediation.invariant_restored: Ensure that no request-supplied text is parsed as a PHP filter specification and that reading the secret file is not reachable from transformed request-controlled output.
mitigation_classes: remove sentinel-gated secret read from request-controlled processing

oracle.expected_negative: An omitted madness value, a value containing a literal slash, an overlength constructed URI, or a value whose transformed result differs from the sentinel should not enter the /flag.txt read branch.
oracle.expected_positive: A candidate GET request that causes the filter result to equal the coded sentinel would cause the handler to render the content read from /flag.txt.
